maria: Heads-up — we started bring-up for Kitewing-10B (community release). License header says "Academic Research Only v0.9" plus an extra clause about "no commercial hosting or redistribution without permission". Looking for guidance on whether we can: run int8 quantization for internal evals, offer it on Dedicated, or allow customers to run it in Private deployments.
kevin: do we have the exact license text? can you paste the paragraph?
maria: pasted below:
```
Academic Research Only v0.9
Permission is granted to use, study and modify for non-commercial research purposes only. Commercial use, hosting, or distribution of model weights, including derivative quantized weights, is prohibited without explicit permission from the copyright holders. Attribution to the original authors is required in any public-facing materials. Export to sanctioned countries may be restricted.
```
amy (legal): quick read — this is a research-only license + explicit hosting/distribution prohibition. Key implications: (1) running internal experiments (evals, quantization research) is allowed if strictly non-commercial, (2) offering the model via our Hosted API would be disallowed (commercial hosting), (3) Dedicated/reserved instances for a paying customer likely count as commercial hosting if we surface the model to them, (4) Private deployments where the customer runs the model on-prem: depends on whether we redistribute weights or merely provide orchestration. If we ship the weights to a customer, that's redistribution and probably disallowed.
kevin: so for Dedicated: even if we control infra, making it available to a paying customer is commercial? even if they have a contract?
amy (legal): yes, the phrase "commercial use, hosting, or distribution" is broad. Unless the copyright holders grant an exception, Dedicated for customers would be risky. For internal Dedicated used only by Redwood teams for benchmarking, that's OK.
sophia: what about producing an int8 derivative for faster inference — is a quantized weight considered a derivative that can't be redistributed?
amy (legal): quantized weights are derivatives. The license explicitly calls out "derivative quantized weights" in the example, so redistribution of those is barred. Internal experiments and eval artifacts are fine.
kevin: any workaround? request a commercial license, or ask upstream to allow redistribution to paying customers under a narrow SLA?
amy (legal): yes — two paths: (A) ask upstream for a commercial sublicense or a redistribution carve-out (they sometimes grant enterprise licenses), (B) avoid redistributing weights: provide a remote inference-only pathway where we don't redistribute weights and the model runs in customer-managed infra — but that still may violate "hosting" depending on contract. We need explicit upstream guidance.
ci-bot: Ticket #ML-3548 created to request upstream licensing clarification from Kitewing authors. Assignee: amy (legal). ETA: 3 business days. :white_check_mark:
maria: noted. Meanwhile can eng run quantized evals in our internal infra and collect quality numbers? want to surface any regressions before we talk to upstream.
sophia: did a quick run — int8 ptq run on our eval set: summarization ROUGE-L dropped 2.3 points, response latency improved ~1.8x. small compliance note: save checkpoints to internal S3 only, mark as research-only.
maria: paste of short eval snippet:
```
model: kitewing-10b-int8-ptq
dataset: news-summ-1k
rouge-l: 0.432 (fp16 baseline 0.455)
latency p50: 220ms -> 120ms
notes: occasional factual hallucinations on long doc (>2k tokens)
```
amy (legal): that eval plan is fine as long as artifacts don't leave our research buckets or get included in customer deliverables. Please tag everything with "research-only" and don't add the quant weights to any deployment images.
kevin: for the engineering side — can we implement a gate in the console to block selection of Kitewing models for Hosted routes until legal says otherwise?
sophia: yep, we can add a quick deny-list entry and flag in model catalog. I'll open PR to hide Kitewing from hosted offerings and allow internal-only flag.
maria: plan: (1) eng runs internal quant evals, (2) amy sends upstream license clarification & asks for a commercial redistribution carve-out, (3) ops hides model from hosted catalog and blocks by default for Dedicated customer-facing pools. Any objections?
amy (legal): sounds good. If upstream grants permission, we'll coordinate terms (attribution wording + export control checks). If not, follow the research-only path.
maria: thanks all. adding follow-ups to the ticket. :sparkles:
